g_notes: SKIP — employee engagement drivers (appreciation, learning, belonging, workplace relationships) is post-hire retention/culture content, explicitly off-limits per brand scope; not a hiring or assessment subject and not a link-worthy format worth transplanting.

angle_gap: Lists 9 generic benefits of pre-employment testing (data-driven hiring, quality of hire, standardization, etc.) using unlinked stat drops ('as per HubSpot', 'as per SHRM') and constant Xobin self-plugs, but never engages the real objections HR leaders raise before adopting testing — validity/adverse-impact risk, candidate drop-off, or how to pick which test type fits which role. No implementation framework, just benefit claims.
asset: The Real Case for Pre-Employment Testing: Benefits Weighed Against the Objections HR Actually Raises
distinct_angle: Pairs each claimed benefit with the specific objection recruiters raise in response (validity, adverse impact, candidate experience) plus a framework for matching test type to role — the pushback-handling and implementation guidance this page skips in favor of one-line benefit claims.

angle_gap: For each white-collar skill cluster (communication, problem-solving, domain knowledge, digital literacy) the page only names the assessment TYPE in one line ('cognitive aptitude tests, case studies, situational judgment assessments') with no sample question, scoring rubric, or example of what a strong vs weak response looks like — a recruiter still can't run the evaluation after reading it.
asset: The White-Collar Skills Employers Actually Need to Test in 2026, With a Sample Question for Each
distinct_angle: Turns each skill cluster's one-line 'how to evaluate' into a worked example — a sample assessment item and what a strong vs weak answer looks like — the concrete evaluation guidance this page skips in favor of naming test types.
